subject: Approval requested: ramp protections & early-termination carve-outs for NovaHealth pilot
messages:
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Amanda Lee <amanda.lee@novahealth.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: NovaHealth pilot SOW + ramp request

Amanda — great speaking earlier. Attached is the draft SOW for the 3-month pilot (NovaHealth_SOW_v1.pdf). A couple of things I flagged for your team:

- Ramp schedule: standard pilot assumes growing usage over month 1–3. We usually expect 50% of committed throughput in M1, 80% in M2, and full in M3.
- Early termination: Nova mentioned needing flexibility if the clinical integration stalls. We'd like to understand acceptable opt-out windows and any downsell protections you need.

Can you confirm the ramp cadence you expect and whether you have a minimum spend requirement for the pilot? If Nova requires a firm opt-out within the first 60 days we may need approval for a partial refund/credit structure (non-standard).

Next step: if you can confirm by EOD Thursday, I’ll circulate a redline SOW for signatures.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
D: +1 415-555-0192

Attachment: NovaHealth_SOW_v1.pdf
From: Amanda Lee <amanda.lee@novahealth.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@novahealth.com
Date: 2026-06-15T12:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: NovaHealth pilot SOW + ramp request

Dev — thanks for the doc. High level response:

- Ramp: We expect a conservative pilot: 20% usage in month 1, 60% month 2, then expand to full by month 4. Our engineering timeline is slower due to validation in production.
- Early termination: We need an opt-out through month 2 with standard payment for any consumption to date, and no ongoing commitment beyond that if we choose to stop. We cannot accept a long tail financial commitment for a pilot.

If Redwood can provide a downsell protection (e.g., ability to reduce committed capacity at end of month 2 without penalty) we can sign quickly. Otherwise procurement will push for a one-month cancel.

Best,
Amanda
Director, Clinical Integrations | NovaHealth
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Amanda Lee <amanda.lee@novahealth.com>
Date: 2026-06-16T08:20:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: NovaHealth pilot SOW + ramp request

Jonas / Laura — forwarding Nova's ask. Key points: they want a slower ramp (20% M1, 60% M2, full M4) and an opt-out after month 2 with no ongoing commitment. Amanda is open to a downsell protection alternative (reduce committed cap at M2 instead of full termination).

I flagged this as non-standard from a revenue and capacity planning perspective. If we allow an opt-out, we should limit exposure via:
- Minimum paid usage for the first 90 days (to cover base infra) OR
- A prorated credit policy + 30–60 day notice for termination OR
- A downsell protection that floors at 50% of committed capacity for the remainder of the contract if they opt to downscale after the pilot.

Can we get executive approval to offer either (A) 90-day minimum with 30-day cancellation thereafter, or (B) a downsell floor of 50% with no refund? I’ve attached the original SOW.

Thanks — Dev

Attachment: NovaHealth_SOW_v1.pdf
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-16T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Approval request — NovaHealth pilot: early-term & ramp clause (deal DN-7391)

Evelyn / Laura — 

Need quick exec sign-off on non-standard commercial language for NovaHealth pilot. Deal context: mid-market healthcare ISV, potential for enterprise expansion; pilot ACV ~$48k if fully used, but predicted initial consumption low due to integration work. Sales asks: slow ramp to month 4 and opt-out after month 2. Procurement won’t accept a long tail.

Options I recommend (prefer in this order):
1) Approve a short-term concession: 90-day minimum paid usage (covers M1–M3) with a 30-day written notice to terminate after that period. No refunds; unused prepayments converted to credits usable on future invoices for up to 12 months.
2) Approve a downsell protection: allow opt-out at M2, but require a floor of 50% of committed capacity for the remaining contract term (no refunds).

Risks: Option 1 reduces revenue flexibility but gives clear cost coverage. Option 2 exposes us to customer churn risk but is cleaner legally.

If you approve either, I’ll instruct Legal to insert the clause and we can present SOW_v2 for signature. Need decision by EOD tomorrow to keep the procurement cadence.

--
Jonas Weber
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-17T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Approval request — NovaHealth pilot: early-term & ramp clause (deal DN-7391)

Thanks for the summary, Jonas. After reviewing ACV, strategic fit, and likely expansion motion into their clinical automation group, I approve a constrained concession:

Approved approach (tightened Option 1):
- 90-day paid minimum covering months 1–3 (no refunds).
- Customer may terminate with 30 days' notice after day 90.
- If Nova opts to downscale at month 2, they may reduce committed capacity but will remain liable for at least 50% of the originally agreed monthly commitment for the remainder of the initial 12-month term, unless Legal negotiates a different commercial credit.
- Include a hard cap: concessions apply only to the pilot SOW and not to any subsequent enterprise contract.

Please have Legal prepare the exact clause language and a redline SOW; Dev, proceed to confirm acceptance with Amanda once Legal provides the doc.

Evelyn Hart
COO | Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Amanda Lee <amanda.lee@novahealth.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, procurement@novahealth.com
Date: 2026-06-18T16:30:00-07:00
Subject: Final SOW v2 & approved ramp/early-term language (DN-7391)

Amanda — appreciate the quick turnaround. We received exec approval on a constrained concession set for the pilot. Attached is the redlined SOW (NovaHealth_SOW_v2.pdf) and the proposed clause (Proposed_Ramp_Clause_redline.docx). High level: 90-day paid minimum (M1–M3), 30-day termination notice after day 90, and a 50% floor if they elect to downscale in M2. This concession applies only to the pilot SOW.

If that reads OK to Nova, I’ll get Legal to prep the final SOW and send a DocuSign link (we’ll include the one-off concession as an addendum). Please confirm acceptance by EOD Monday and I’ll route to signature.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
